data.narrative:
Lambda, a Series E AI & Software company that has raised $3.15B to date, operates within a sector containing 1 public comparable (Palantir) and 8 private peers including Figure AI, Scale AI, and Applied Intuition. The peer set, however, lacks sufficient narrow-filter matches to support a reliable peer-median valuation method; only 1 adjacent-stage comparable was identified, falling short of the 3-datapoint threshold needed for statistical credibility.

The stage-progression method is the primary applicable triangulation approach. Using total capital raised ($3.1B) as a valuation proxy and applying a typical 1.4x step-up multiplier for Series E advancement yields an implied valuation of $4.4B. This method assumes that Lambda's next-stage financing will follow standard venture progression patterns observed across the AI & Software sector.

Given limited methodology diversity, the analysis triangulates to a median of $4.4B with a low-to-high range of $3.7B to $5.1B. This range reflects valuation support from stage-progression mechanics alone. Key uncertainties include the absence of directly comparable Series E AI & Software transactions and the reliance on a single empirical method. Any post-Series E valuation should be revisited as peer-stage data becomes available or as Lambda approaches its next financing event.
